answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with the lock period extending past settlement. A mirror check links repeated claims to the same stake, while a ridge of accumulated reputation raises the minimum bond for high-value jobs. If an agent defaults or is proven to double-vote, the protocol slashes its bond. Creating many identities therefore multiplies capital tied up and exposed to loss; a ferrous-sounding profile alone buys no influence.
